Sheep castration guide: closed castration with the Burdizzo

A bloodless technique: the elements of the spermatic cord are crushed through intact skin, so the testis atrophies without any open wound. A study guide for Special Surgery before hands-on training.

  • No skin wound
  • Lower risk of fly strike and infection
  • Breeding and aggression control
  • Improved meat quality

Introduction

This platform teaches closed castration in sheep with the Burdizzo. It brings together the animated procedure, 2D and 3D anatomy, the instruments in order of use, the outcome over time, aftercare, quizzes and a reference list.

It is written for veterinary students, clinical teachers and practising veterinarians. It is educational material: practise under supervision and follow local animal welfare law.

How to use this platform

  1. Pick a part. Use the menu at the top or the Contents below. Each part opens on its own page.
  2. Follow the procedure. In Procedure, use the numbered steps, Back, Next or Autoplay. Switch between 2D and 3D and drag the model to rotate it.
  3. Explore the anatomy. Select a layer, or peel the layers in 3D.
  4. Search. Type a word such as septum or tetanus in the search box and pick a result. Press / to jump to the search box.
  5. Test yourself. Take the quizzes, then check the references.

The Burdizzo crushes from outside the skin: the testicular artery, pampiniform plexus, ductus deferens and nerves are damaged while the skin stays intact.

Instruments and supplies

The instruments in the order they are used. Press Show in animation to jump to that step.

  1. 1
    Before step 1Tetanus prophylaxis toxoid or antitoxinPlan ahead: extension guidance suggests toxoid at least 2 weeks before castration, with antitoxin if the dam was unvaccinated. The technique is closed, but the risk remains.
  2. 2
    Step 1Assistant and restraintSecures the animal and exposes the hindquarters safely.
  3. 3
    Step 1Gloves and record sheetFor recording age and date, and for examining both testes before and after.
  4. 4
    Step 2Antiseptic povidone-iodine or chlorhexidineFor scrotal skin and for the jaws of the instrument.
  5. 5
    Before the crushLocal anesthetic and analgesic lidocaine, NSAIDGiven according to the supervising veterinarian’s protocol. Local anesthesia reduces distress but does not remove post-operative pain responses.
  6. 6
    Steps 4 and 5Burdizzo bloodless emasculatomeMust be clean, in good condition, with aligned jaws. Its jaws crush the isolated spermatic cord without cutting the skin and are held closed for roughly 10 to 25 seconds depending on the guidance (Refs 6, 12).
  7. 7
    Step 6Burdizzo again second cordRepeated on the opposite cord, at a different level, then the animal is monitored.

Application

Comparison of the closed methods

FeatureBurdizzoRubber ringRing + Burdizzo
PrincipleCrushes each spermatic cord through intact skinRing at the scrotal neck cuts off blood supply (Ref 10)Ring at the scrotal neck, then a clamp across the full width of the neck up to the ring's outer edge (Ref 10)
WoundNo skin wound; no wound infection or fly problems (Ref 3)Scrotum and testes drop off in about 2 to 4 weeks, leaving a granulating wound (Refs 3, 10)Same sloughing as the ring (Ref 10)
Age and lawCheck local lawEngland: lambs 7 days or younger (Ref 10)Lambs 1 to 7 days old, not in the first 24 hours (Ref 10)
WelfareFewer pain-related behaviours than ring or short-scrotum (Ref 10); healed faster than ring in lambs over 10 weeks (Ref 13)Slower healing; pain-related behaviours reported up to 6 weeks (Ref 10)Fewer pain-related behaviours than ring alone (Ref 10)
Main riskIncomplete castration; incomplete involution is common in lambs (Refs 1, 3)Cannot be used on cryptorchids; teats must stay outside the ring (Ref 10)Mismothering if done too early (Ref 10)
All methodsVaccinate against tetanus beforehand, ideally at least 2 weeks (Ref 11). Local anaesthesia reduced behavioural and cortisol responses in lambs aged 2 to 7 days (Ref 14).

Teaching model: sheep hindquarters

A low-cost anatomical model of the ram's hindquarters and scrotal contents, built to rehearse positioning, cord isolation and Burdizzo placement before work on live animals. This page documents the materials, the build, and the anatomical purpose of each part.

1. Materials and tools

ComponentMaterialsFunction in the model
Base and bodyWooden board, sponge blocks, glue, fabric, cottonStable base; abdominal and perineal mass; wool-like surface texture
Hind limbsWooden skewers, metal pieces, heat-moldable clay, glue, cottonLimb framework with adjustable joint angles; hooves (claws) shaped in clay
Testes and epididymisBalloon filled with cotton, a piece of red electrical sleeve, rubber bandsTestis and epididymis with realistic shape and feel
Spermatic cordsIV giving-set tubing cut at both ends, plastic hub of a needleCords linking each testis to the body; the hub joins the second cord to its testis
ScrotumWhite fabric (inner sac), black fabric (outer cover)Two-layer scrotal covering
Working toolsHot-glue gun, scissors, needle and thread, skewersCutting, stitching, fixing and shaping the parts

2. Construction steps

Step 1. Body and abdomen

Glue the sponge blocks together and fix them to the wooden base so the model stays stable during practice. Stitch the sponge where needed, then cover it with fabric and a layer of cotton to reproduce the shape and texture of the ventral abdomen.

Purpose: a firm, stable mass that holds the cords and scrotum in a realistic position.

Step 2. Hind limbs

Build the limb framework from wooden skewers and metal pieces, setting the joint angles before fixing them with glue and heat-moldable clay. Cover the frame with cotton and shape the hooves at the distal ends.

Purpose: limbs that can be abducted, so the model can be positioned in dorsal recumbency with the scrotum exposed, as in restraint practice.

Step 3. Testes, epididymis and cords

Fill a balloon with cotton to form each testis, and add a segment of red electrical sleeve with rubber bands to form the epididymis below it. Cut both ends of the IV tubing: tie one end to the first testis, and tie the other end to the plastic hub of a needle that connects to the second testis.

Purpose: palpable testes and a cord that can be isolated, pushed to one side and clamped.

Step 4. Scrotal covering and final assembly

Wrap each testis in white fabric as the inner sac, then cover both in black fabric as the outer scrotal skin. Pass the tubing into the body and position the scrotum between the abducted hind limbs.

Purpose: a two-layer scrotum through which the cord can be located by touch, as in the clinical exam.

4. Suggested improvements

Anatomical accuracy

  • Use the platform colour code: testis pink, epididymis tan, cord red, ductus deferens cream, pampiniform plexus violet.
  • Show the ductus deferens as a separate thin tube beside the thicker cord, with a violet wrap for the plexus near the testis.
  • Add a stitched fabric septum between the two testes, so students practise keeping it out of the jaws.
  • Sew the two scrotal layers separately, with an elastic neck that can be gathered.

Function for Burdizzo practice

  • Use soft silicone tubing for the cords, so a cord can be pushed laterally and clamped.
  • Make the cords replaceable through sleeves, so the model can be reused after each crush.
  • Fill a clear tube with coloured water or gel, so a crush is visible when the tube is clamped.
  • Mark the recommended crush zone on the scrotal neck with a removable marker.

Durability and safety

  • Remove sharp props such as the scalpel blade from the practice area.
  • Use a non-slip pad under the base and a washable outer cover.
  • Label the model as educational only.

Documentation

  • Record the dimensions and a bill of materials, and photograph each stage.
  • Give each build a version number.
  • Use the skill checklist in For educators to assess practice on the model.

Limits: the model has no real tissue elasticity, bleeding or animal behaviour, and it is not to scale. It supports positioning and technique rehearsal only.

Comparison and complications

The choice of method depends on age, facilities and the animal’s welfare.

MethodWoundAdvantageNote
Burdizzo (closed)NonePractically bloodlessFails if the cord is not fully crushed
Elastrator ringNone, then necrosis and sloughingFast and simpleYoung lambs; longer pain and higher tetanus risk
Open surgical orchiectomyScrotal incisionReliable at any ageNeeds anesthesia, asepsis and wound care
  • Incomplete castration: the cord was not crushed properly, so re-examine the scrotum after a few weeks.
  • Scrotal skin necrosis: from crushing skin too hard, or crushing both cords at the same level.
  • Transient scrotal swelling, which needs monitoring.
  • Tetanus, pain and stress: plan prophylaxis, analgesia and calm handling.

Aftercare and follow-up

Closed castration still needs monitoring. Use this timeline for the flock record.

  1. First 24 to 48 hoursKeep animals in a clean, dry area. Mild scrotal swelling is expected. Check appetite, gait and any straining.
  2. First weekLook for heat, severe pain, discharge or flies at the scrotum. Call the veterinarian if swelling keeps increasing. Watch for stiffness as an early sign of tetanus.
  3. Weeks 4 to 6Re-examine: the testes should be shrinking and firm, and the cord should not be palpable. A normal-sized testis means failed castration and needs repeating.
  4. RecordsNote date, age, operator, any complications and the result of the re-examination.

For educators and clinicians

Teaching and assessment aids for veterinary programmes, clinical instruction and continuing education.

Learning outcomes

  • Describe the layers of the scrotum and the contents of the spermatic cord in the ram.
  • Justify the choice between Burdizzo, banding and surgical castration for a given animal, age and setting.
  • Sequence the closed-castration steps, including cord isolation and the level of the crush.
  • Recognise incomplete castration and other complications, and plan follow-up.
  • Apply welfare principles: analgesia, handling and local legal limits.

Discussion prompts

  • Histology showed incomplete involution in most lambs after Burdizzo castration (Ref 1). What does this mean for owner counselling and follow-up?
  • Which factors could affect crush completeness: age, cord thickness, level, hold time, instrument condition?
  • Compare Burdizzo and banding for pain, complications and failure (Refs 2, 5, 7).
  • When is surgical castration the better choice?

Welfare and regulation

  • Age limits, who may perform castration, and analgesia rules differ by country and change over time; check local law. For example, Irish guidance limits non-veterinary Burdizzo use in cattle by age (Ref 6).
  • Local anesthesia and analgesics are discussed in the welfare literature as ways to reduce pain (Ref 7).
  • One source regards the emasculatome as a very inhumane method (Ref 5), so justify the method and record the decision.

Evidence gaps

  • Most quantitative data come from cattle; sheep-specific histology is limited.
  • The ideal crush level, hold time and age for lambs are not firmly established in the sources found.
  • The outcome timeline in this guide is illustrative; replace it with your own data where available.

For supervised practice or an OSCE-style station. Tick each criterion as it is shown correctly.
